statement: Find the point(s) on the parabola $y=x^{2}$ that are closest to $(0,2)$, and state the minimum distance.
solution: Distance squared to $(0,2)$ is $D=x^{2}+(x^{2}-2)^{2}=x^{4}-3x^{2}+4$. $D'=4x^{3}-6x=2x(2x^{2}-3)=0$ gives $x=0$ or $x^{2}=3/2$. At $x=0$, $D=4$ (distance $2$). At $x^{2}=3/2$, $D=(9/4)-3(3/2)+4=7/4$, distance $\sqrt{7}/2\approx1.323<2$. So the closest points are $\left(\pm\sqrt{3/2},\,3/2\right)$ and the minimum distance is $\sqrt{7}/2$.
hints: Minimise the squared distance to avoid square roots.
Set the derivative of $x^{4}-3x^{2}+4$ to zero.
